source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #273 (branch fix/171-metering-jit at head ba31ed1bd15d823b43f51e2051b0146a72c94b6e — branch commit 4c9646d (execution metering covers JIT-compiled execution) plus merge commit ba31ed1 bringing in current main 6373f8c, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45160924686 and 45160938599 against the branch and pull-request run 45160922321, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #273 (#171, execution metering covers JIT-compiled execution: the store normalisation that disabled the JIT under metering is removed, a metered flag is threaded through the compile path into the JIT emitters, native metering checkpoints are emitted at guest loop headers and at the four fused loops’ back-edges in all three backends, a new MeteringCheckpoint stub refills or raises through vm::checkpoint, and the bulk-memory, table and shared-notify stubs charge with exactly the interpreter’s formulas and ordering). The branch merged current main (6373f8c, the PR #269 squash merge) before measurement, so the first CI run on the merged tree tripped the gate on the PR’s own change. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (6373f8c) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45160951447, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta is this PR’s own. The growth is confined to core-jit, the only configuration that links the JIT emitters and stubs (release stripped file +6,280 B / stripped .text +5,248 B; release-size stripped file +4,744 B / stripped .text +3,840 B): the per-backend checkpoint emitters, the MeteringCheckpoint stub and the stub charge calls. Instrumentation is emitted only for metered stores, so code compiled for unmetered stores is byte-identical; what grows is the runtime’s own code. In the release profile the other library configurations shrink slightly (stripped file and stripped .text −144 B in core, component, wasi, core-nosimd and wasi-threads; −176 B in core-aot), the code-layout effect of removing the metering/JIT normalisation block from the store constructor. In release-size every configuration except core-jit is byte-identical, and the baseline configuration is unchanged in both profiles; 16 of the 32 gated series change. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release-size component stripped .text series at +5.41% (1,169,031 B to 1,232,263 B), unchanged from after PR #269, because that series does not move in this PR. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (16 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3; the raw file and .text sizes were also identical across the three runs), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’.
